summary: Kickoff for Lumen Therapy onboarding to Redwood. Goals: migrate inference for chat assistants to Dedicated or Private deployment, meet latency SLOs for consumer app, confirm security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and schedule technical deep dive to validate VPC network setup and benchmark plan.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Patel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, welcome. I think we have about 45 minutes, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:06 Emily Park (Lumen): Emily here, Head of ML Ops.
00:09 Carlos Rivera (Lumen): Carlos, CTO.
:11 Samir Singh (Lumen): Samir, platform.
00:14 Maya Chen (Redwood SE): Maya from Redwood, good to meet you all. Priya from CS is on the call but muted.
00:22 Jordan: Great. The agenda — quick intros, high level goals for onboarding, security/compliance check, deployment options and then agree next steps.
00:33 Emily: Sounds good. For context, Lumen's using a mix today — OpenAI for some customer-facing chat flows and a smaller self-hosted LLM for internal routing. We're trying to centralize to reduce cost and get more predictable latency, and also need to meet healthcare data retention policies.
00:51 Jordan: Perfect. Can you share current volume and latency targets?
00:54 Emily: We're about 800-1,200 requests per minute peak, average token length is around 120 tokens per request, and target p95 latency under 400 ms for generation. We also have spikes up to 2k RPS during promo windows.
01:12 Maya: Got it. Quick clarifying q: when you say 400 ms p95, is that end-to-end or server-side generation only?
01:18 Carlos: End-to-end as visible in the app, so networking included. We can tolerate some regional routing but need consistent response for east/west coast.
01:27 Maya: Okay that helps. For Dedicated vs Private, two main things we'll evaluate: predictable throughput (reserved GPU pools) and network controls (VPC peering/PrivateLink). If you need full on-prem we also support air-gapped private package but that's a heavier lift.
01:46 Samir: For data residency and SOC2, we need audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO (SAML). Is that in place?
01:54 Jordan: Yes — Redwood supports SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS via customer-managed keys, and audit logs. We can share the SOC2 doc and our security whitepaper after the call.
02:06 Emily: Great. Can you also confirm retention policies? We can't keep PII in logs beyond 30 days without a defined process.
02:14 Priya Rao (Redwood CSM) [muted then unmuted]: We typically configure short retention policies per account and can route logs to customer KMS-backed storage. I'll follow up with the exact defaults and options.
02:29 Jordan: For the migration path, customers commonly pilot on Hosted with specific models to validate quality and then move to Dedicated for throughput. Given your 2k spike and strict latency, Dedicated or Private is probably where you'll land. But we should run a benchmark to confirm unit economics.
02:46 Carlos: Cost is a big driver. We need predictable monthly spend for forecasting. Reserved capacity sounds promising.
02:52 Maya: Yep, Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with autoscale and burst options. You can pin model versions and we provide token-level cost breakdowns in the Console so finance can see it.
03:05 Emily: One more thing — we use a private VPC and NATing rules. Do you support cross-account VPC peering or PrivateLink?
03:12 Maya: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on cloud provider; our Private deployment offers a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC. We'll need network team to open a few ports and set up peering. Samir, we'll need your network CIDRs.
03:26 Samir: I'll share our network diagram. Also we use strict outbound rules so please note, some of your agents might require egress for model updates?
03:34 Jordan: For the Private package yes there is an optional update path; for air-gapped we do manual updates. We'll document the update cadence.
03:42 Carlos: On benchmarks, can Redwood run a sample test with our payload to validate latency and KV cache behavior? We rely on long-context docs per user so KV caching will be important.
03:52 Maya: Absolutely. We'll set up a benchmark plan: we'd like a sample traffic trace from you (Samir) and a few prompt templates. We'll test with cache enabled vs cold start. That will give us expected token cost and p95 latency.
04:08 Jordan: Action item: Samir to send traffic profile and a set of typical prompts. Maya to prepare benchmark plan.
04:16 Emily: About security, SOC2 and ISO — can you provide the certs and also do you do penetration testing reports?
04:22 Jordan: Yes, SOC2 report and pen test summaries we can share under an NDA. We'll put links in the follow up email.
04:31 Emily: Good. Also need clarity on data deletion APIs and ability to prevent retention of raw text.
04:37 Priya: There are account-level settings plus we have programmatic APIs to scrub logs. We'll include docs.
04:44 Carlos: Who will be our day-to-day contacts? For tech questions and escalation.
04:48 Jordan: Jordan for commercial, Priya for onboarding/CS, Maya for technical and benchmark lead.
04:54 Samir: Timeline question — we are aiming for a production pilot in 6 weeks, full rollout in 12 weeks. Is that feasible?
05:01 Maya: That seems reasonable. Typical onboarding (pilot) is 4-8 weeks depending on changes. If Private deployment required that can add a few weeks for network approvals.
05:13 Jordan: We'll aim for a pilot in 6 weeks. For cost modeling, we'll provide an initial estimate after benchmark results.
05:20 Emily: Any gotchas you typically see?
05:23 Maya: Common ones: token distribution mismatch (if your average tokens are higher than test prompts, cost jumps), KV cache tuning for long docs, and model quantization tradeoffs that can affect quality. We'll flag those after the benchmark.
05:36 Samir: On the auth side, we need SAML metadata and SCIM user provisioning. Do you support SCIM?
05:41 Jordan: Yes SCIM provisioning is supported. We'll include the SAML/SCIM integration guide.
05:47 Emily: Can you also send a sample SLA for Dedicated? We need uptime and latency SLOs for procurement.
05:52 Jordan: Yes, I'll attach our Dedicated SLA and the typical uptime/latency targets we commit to.
05:59 Carlos: Competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and AWS endpoints. Price/perf was mixed; interested to see Redwood's Dedicated numbers.
06:08 Maya: Understood. We'll benchmark similarly to provide apples-to-apples.
06:13 Priya: Quick note — I'll create a project in our onboarding tracker with tasks and invite Emily, Carlos, Samir. That will include the kickoff notes and action owners.
06:23 Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan sends deck, pricing and SLA; Maya and Samir schedule technical deep dive and Maya prepares benchmark plan; Samir sends traffic profile and prompts; Priya sets up onboarding workspace and shares SOC2/pen test docs under NDA.
06:40 Emily: That works. Thanks team.
06:42 Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials by EOD tomorrow.
06:46 Carlos: Thanks. Bye.
06:47 Meeting ends
